questionText: What is the difference between application.properties and application.yml?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can express equivalent Spring settings in properties and YAML and choose a format based on readability without inventing a capability difference.

claims.statement: Spring Boot loads properties and YAML config data into equivalent Environment property keys even though one syntax is flat and the other represents nested structures with indentation.
When a properties file and a YAML file with the same base name exist in the same config-data location, Spring Boot gives the .properties file precedence.

examples.title: Load the exact properties and YAML client settings independently

validation.command: Run separate Spring Boot 3.3.1 contexts with the exact learner .properties and .yml documents and assert all scalar and indexed list keys
validation.expected: Both documents expose the same base URL, two-second timeout, and two ordered regions

visuals.title: Properties and YAML compared by syntax, lists, risks, and Spring result

notes: The two code fences are separate valid formats rather than a mixed-language block.

review.notes: Format equivalence, YAML loading, list flattening, and same-location precedence were checked against official Spring Boot documentation; both exact examples loaded successfully.
